title_en: China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd. v. COSCO Shipping Co., Ltd., and Third Parties Hainan Branch and Hainan FAW Haima Automobile Sales Co., Ltd. — dispute over compensation for cargo damage under a contract of carriage of goods by water
ruling_gist_en: The Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, as a special law, shall prevail in the trial of disputes over contracts of carriage of goods by sea. Pursuant to Article 2, paragraph 2 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, the provisions of Chapter IV of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China shall not apply to the carriage of goods by sea between ports of the People's Republic of China, including carriage of goods on inland waters and along the coast, and the relevant provisions of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China shall apply.

full_text_en:
China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd. v. COSCO Shipping Co., Ltd. and Hainan Branch, Hainan FAW Haima Automobile Sales Co., Ltd. — dispute over cargo damage compensation in a waterway cargo transport contract

[Ruling Summary]

The Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, as a special law, shall prevail in the trial of disputes over contracts for the carriage of goods by sea. Pursuant to Article 2, paragraph 2 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, the provisions of Chapter 4 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China shall not apply to the carriage of goods by sea between ports of the People's Republic of China, including the carriage of goods by inland waterway and coastal waters, and the relevant provisions of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China shall apply instead.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2011) Min Ti Zi No. 12

Reapplying Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): COSCO Shipping Co., Ltd. Domicile: Kangsheng Building, No. 282 Dongjiang Avenue, Free Trade Zone, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Xu Lirong, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Jiachun, lawyer of Beijing Tianda Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Han Cuijing, lawyer of Beijing Tianda Law Firm.

Reapplying Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd. Hainan Branch. Domicile: Huaneng Building, No. 36 Datong Road, Haikou City, Hainan Province.

Person in Charge: Xiang Yong, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Ren Yanbing, lawyer of Guangdong Hengfu Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liang Yonggang, lawyer of Guangdong Hengfu Law Firm.

Third Party at First Instance: Hainan FAW Haima Automobile Sales Co., Ltd. Domicile: Jinpan Industrial Development Zone, Haikou City, Hainan Province.

Legal Representative: Wu Shaoming, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Chen Yong, male, Han nationality, born on June 15, 1982, staff member of Hainan FAW Haima Automobile Sales Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 2 Jinniu Road, Longhua District, Haikou City, Hainan Province.

In the case of dispute over cargo damage compensation under a contract for the carriage of goods by water between reapplying applicant COSCO Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as COSCO Company) and reapplying respondent China Pacific Property Insurance Co., Ltd. Hainan Branch (hereinafter referred to as CPIC Hainan Company), and third party at first instance Hainan FAW Haima Automobile Sales Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haima Sales Company), the Hainan High People's Court rendered a civil judgment on March 12, 2010, (2010) Qiong Min San Zhong Zi No. 2, which has become legally effective. COSCO Company, dissatisfied with the judgment, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court decided to hear the case by way of retrial on November 19, 2010, by civil ruling (2010) Min Shen Zi No. 1504. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and heard the case in open court on February 11, 2011. Zhang Jiachun and Han Cuijing, agents ad litem of reapplying applicant COSCO Company, Ren Yanbing, agent ad litem of reapplying respondent CPIC Hainan Company, and Chen Yong, agent ad litem of third party at first instance Haima Sales Company, appeared in court. The trial of this case is now concluded.

CPIC Hainan Company filed a lawsuit to the first instance Haikou Maritime Court, alleging: On January 1, 2007, Hainan Jinpan Logistics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinpan Logistics Company), on behalf of Haima Sales Company, signed the "Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement" with COSCO Company. On December 17, 2007, the vessel "Fuyuankou" of COSCO Company loaded 610 Haima brand commercial vehicles owned by Haima Sales Company, and sailed from Haikou to Shanghai. Haima Sales Company also insured this batch of vehicles with CPIC Hainan Company for waterway transportation insurance. On December 23, 2007, when the above commercial vehicles arrived in Shanghai, it was found that most of the vehicles were severely damaged. CPIC Hainan Company paid a total of RMB 16,395,960 in insurance claims to Haima Sales Company, and also paid other related expenses of RMB 807,804. It requested a judgment: 1. COSCO Company to compensate for the insurance claim, other expenses, and interest on the above two losses; 2. COSCO Company to bear the litigation costs of this case and other related expenses incurred as a result of the litigation.

COSCO Company defended at first instance: 1. The party that signed the waterway transport contract with COSCO Company was Jinpan Logistics Company, not Haima Sales Company; CPIC Hainan Company lacked standing and had no right to exercise subrogation rights; 2. The fire accident in question was caused by spontaneous combustion of the vehicle, and the carrier was not liable; 3. The amount of cargo damage claimed by CPIC Hainan Company was untrue and unreasonable; 4. Even if COSCO Company was liable for compensation, it should only be liable within the limitation of maritime liability. Before the hearing, COSCO Company submitted to Haikou Maritime Court an "Application for Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims," requesting the limitation amount of RMB 7,900,000.

The facts found by the first instance Haikou Maritime Court were as follows: The "Agreement" signed between Haima Sales Company and Jinpan Logistics Company on December 31, 2006, stipulated that Haima Sales Company entrusted the logistics, warehousing, and transportation of Haima commercial vehicles to Jinpan Logistics Company, and Jinpan Logistics Company was responsible for the logistics, warehousing, and transportation of Haima commercial vehicles entrusted by Haima Sales Company; Jinpan Logistics Company was to insure the automobile products sold by Haima Sales Company, including transportation insurance and warehousing insurance; in the event of an insured accident during the transportation or warehousing of automobile products, Jinpan Logistics Company was to conduct claim work. On January 1, 2007, Jinpan Logistics Company and COSCO Company signed the "Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement," under which Jinpan Logistics Company designated COSCO Company as the carrier for waterway transportation of vehicles from Haikou to Shanghai, and COSCO Company was to use its ro-ro vessels to carry out the waterway transportation of vehicles for Jinpan Logistics Company from Haikou to Shanghai. Article 17, paragraph 8 of the agreement stipulated that if, due to non-exemptible reasons, COSCO Company breached the agreement and caused losses to Jinpan Logistics Company or the vehicle manufacturer, Jinpan Logistics Company or the vehicle manufacturer had the right to claim compensation. Article 22, paragraph 1 provided that "vehicle manufacturer" means the manufacturer of the vehicles or the enterprise responsible for the sales management of the vehicles. According to the "Exclusive Distributor Agreement," Haima Sales Company was the owner of the vehicles in question. On December 16, 2007, Jinpan Logistics Company insured the subject goods under a basic waterway transportation insurance policy, with CPIC Hainan Company as the insurer and Haima Sales Company as the insured, covering 610 Haima brand sedans, transported by the vessel "Fuyuankou," departing from Haikou Xiuying Wharf and arriving at Shanghai Haitong Wharf. On December 17 of the same year, the vessel "Fuyuankou" owned by COSCO Company loaded 611 Haima brand sedans (including 1 test vehicle) owned by Haima Sales Company and transported them from Haikou to Shanghai. All of the above vehicles had vehicle qualification certificates, proving that the vehicles carried by "Fuyuankou" were new vehicles manufactured by FAW Haima Automobile Co., Ltd., which had undergone strict mandatory tests (including road tests, etc.) before leaving the factory, and could guarantee safety for any possible conditions during driving and transportation (including possible bumps and vibrations). The "Marine Incident Report" and "Deck Log Book" of the vessel in question proved that at approximately 0950 hours on December 21, 2007, when sailing near the Zhoushan Islands, a fire broke out in the cargo hold on board. The ship immediately organized the crew to extinguish the fire. At approximately 0823-0835 hours on December 22, 2007, after sending crew members into the hold to detect the fire, it was confirmed that the fire had been extinguished. On December 23 at 1700 hours, the vessel arrived at Shanghai Haitong Wharf. The fire covered a wide area, and the center and its affected area reached high temperatures, even causing deformation of the deck. A total of 462 vehicles were involved in the fire. To facilitate accident handling and vehicle inspection, the parties agreed to return the vehicles involved to Haikou. Thereafter, the insured Haima Sales Company and insurer CPIC Hainan Company reached an "Insurance Compensation Agreement" on April 10, 2008, confirming that CPIC Hainan Company would pay Haima Sales Company RMB 16,395,960 in compensation for the damaged Haima commercial vehicles in question, including RMB 1,000,000 advanced by CPIC Hainan Company to the policyholder Jinpan Logistics Company on February 3, 2008; the salvage costs incurred before the agreement took effect (cleaning fees, venue fees, storage fees, return shipping fees) were to be paid separately by CPIC Hainan Company to Jinpan Logistics Company; after the agreement took effect, Haima Sales Company agreed to transfer its rights of recourse against third parties to CPIC Hainan Company. On April 24 of the same year, CPIC Hainan Company transferred RMB 15,395,960 to Haima Sales Company, and Haima Sales Company issued a receipt for the compensation to CPIC Hainan Company.

After the occurrence of the insured accident, the vessel "Fuyuankou" did not report the fire to the fire authority or apply for an investigation into the cause of the fire. To ascertain the cause of the fire in question, CPIC Hainan Company and COSCO Company separately commissioned appraisals regarding the cause of the fire. CPIC Hainan Company commissioned China Certification & Inspection Group Shanghai Co., Ltd. to conduct an appraisal, which issued an "Inspection Report" concluding that the fire accident on "Fuyuankou" was caused by factors other than the vehicle itself. COSCO Company commissioned Zhejiang Entry-Exit Inspection and Quarantine Appraisal Institute (Zhejiang CIQ Appraisal Institute) to conduct an appraisal, which issued a "Forensic Appraisal Report" concluding that the fire accident in question was caused by spontaneous combustion of the vehicle itself; COSCO Company commissioned Shanghai Yuezhi Insurance Surveyors and Loss Adjusters Co., Ltd. to conduct an appraisal, which issued a "Survey Report" concluding that the fire accident in question was caused by spontaneous combustion of the vehicle itself; COSCO Company commissioned Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd. to conduct an appraisal, which issued an "Inspection Report" concluding that the fire accident in question was caused by spontaneous combustion of the vehicle itself. Upon review, the institutions that issued the above opinions on the cause of the fire did not have public management functions, nor did they have the qualifications or business scope for fire investigation and determination.

CPIC Hainan Company, COSCO Company, and Haima Sales Company each provided evidence to prove the losses caused by the fire in question. CPIC Hainan Company, to prove its losses, provided the "Inspection Report on 19 Damaged Haima Commercial Vehicles in the 'Fuyuankou' Accident," the "Inspection Report on 443 Damaged Haima Commercial Vehicles in the 'Fuyuankou' Accident," and the "Loss Assessment Report on Vehicles Carried by 'Fuyuankou'" as main evidence, proving that according to the inspection by the Quality Management Department of the vehicle manufacturer FAW Haima Automobile Co., Ltd. in accordance with relevant product quality and inspection standards, the fire accident in question resulted in total loss of 19 vehicles and serious loss or damage to 443 vehicles among the vehicles carried by "Fuyuankou"; according to the assessment by its Operation Management Department, the loss amount of the vehicles carried by 'Fuyuankou' due to the fire accident was RMB 27,860,950. The third party Haima Sales Company also provided the same evidence. Additionally, CPIC Hainan Company commissioned the Haikou Price Certification Center to assess the losses. The Center, which had the qualifications for price appraisal, issued a "Price Appraisal Report" concluding that the loss amount of the vehicles carried by 'Fuyuankou' due to the fire accident was RMB 16,797,902. China Certification & Inspection Group Shanghai Co., Ltd. issued an "Inspection Report" concluding that the extent of damage and residual value of the damaged vehicles in the fire accident was RMB 21,809,698. This company did not have price appraisal qualifications, and the relevant loss figures cited the determinations in the "Price Appraisal Report" issued by the Haikou Price Certification Center. To prove the actual disposal of the vehicles in question, Haima Sales Company provided the sales contracts and invoices for the actual disposal after repair of the damaged vehicles in question, proving that the total sales price of 444 damaged vehicles (including 1 test vehicle) after repair was RMB 19,245,400. COSCO Company separately commissioned Zhejiang CIQ Appraisal Institute and Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd. to conduct appraisals. The "Forensic Appraisal Report" issued by Zhejiang CIQ Appraisal Institute proved that the total loss amount of the damaged vehicles should be RMB 4,597,340, and the business scope of this institute did not include price appraisal. Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd., which had price appraisal qualifications, issued an "Inspection Report" concluding that the loss amount of the damaged vehicles should be RMB 4,566,500. Mr. Huang Yaquan, Director of Guangdong Hengyun Law Firm, where the agent ad litem of COSCO Company practiced, was the largest shareholder of Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd., and Mr. Huang Yaquan had previously been commissioned by COSCO Company to send a "Declaration" to Jinpan Logistics Company and CPIC Hainan Company on March 5, 2008, regarding the handling of the fire accident in question. After the fire accident occurred, CPIC Hainan Company, in order to determine the nature, cause, and extent of the insured accident, as well as to carry out salvage and handling of the damaged vehicles, in consultation with COSCO Company, returned the damaged vehicles from Shanghai to Haikou, incurring wharf storage fees of RMB 321,618, handling and detailing fees of RMB 132,200, cleaning fees of RMB 97,240, transfer fees of RMB 13,230, guarding fees of RMB 20,900, appraisal and evaluation fees of RMB 107,700 (RMB 32,700 + RMB 75,000), and evidence preservation fees of RMB 5,000 incurred before litigation to preserve evidence, totaling RMB 697,888.

It was also found that according to the "Regulations on the Administration of Old Transport Vessels" promulgated by the Ministry of Communications in 2006, although "Fuyuankou" was an old vessel, it was a Class V old seagoing ship, and its compulsory decommissioning period was 34 years or more. At the time of the fire accident, the vessel was only 25 years old, far from reaching the compulsory decommissioning age. "Fuyuankou" held various valid seaworthiness certificates, including a Certificate of Ship's Nationality, Cargo Ship Safety Construction Certificate, Cargo Ship Safety Equipment Certificate, Safety Management Certificate, Hull and Machinery Classification Certificate, Ship Annual Inspection Certificate, and Minimum Safe Manning Certificate. In the absence of other contrary evidence, it was determined that "Fuyuankou" was seaworthy. According to the Certificate of Ship's Nationality and Certificate of Ship's Ownership of "Fuyuankou," the vessel had a gross tonnage of 8,553 tons, and its approved scope of business was the water transportation of complete commercial vehicles between ports in domestic coastal waters and the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River. On October 23, 2009, the conversion rate of Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) to RMB as announced by the International Monetary Fund was 1 SDR = RMB 10.9057.

Based on the facts of this case, the Haikou Maritime Court at first instance analyzed and determined the disputed issues as follows:

(1) Regarding the issue of CPIC Hainan Company's standing. The "Agreement" signed between Haima Sales Company and Jinpan Logistics Company on December 31, 2006, conforms to the provisions of Article 403 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and is a mandate contract in nature, with Jinpan Logistics Company as the agent and Haima Sales Company as the principal. On January 1, 2007, the "Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement" signed between Jinpan Logistics Company and COSCO Company was in fact signed by Jinpan Logistics Company on behalf of Haima Sales Company with COSCO Company. Moreover, according to the vehicle transport cooperation agreements for 2004, 2005, 2006, and 2008 provided by the third party Haima Sales Company and COSCO Company, COSCO Company had been cooperating with Jinpan Logistics Company in this manner since 2004. Therefore, COSCO Company should have been well aware of the relationship between Jinpan Logistics Company and Haima Sales Company, and the agency status of Jinpan Logistics Company. COSCO Company claimed that if it had known that the principal was Haima Sales Company, it would not have signed the contract with Jinpan Logistics Company, but did not provide corresponding evidence to prove this. Therefore, the fact that there existed a contract for the carriage of goods by water between Haima Sales Company and COSCO Company, as claimed by CPIC Hainan Company, is affirmed.

On December 16, 2007, Jinpan Logistics Company insured the subject goods under a basic waterway transportation insurance policy, with CPIC Hainan Company as the insurer and Haima Sales Company as the insured. After the fire accident, the insured Haima Sales Company and the insurer CPIC Hainan Company reached an "Insurance Compensation Agreement." On April 24, 2008, CPIC Hainan Company transferred RMB 15,395,960 to Haima Sales Company, and Haima Sales Company issued a receipt for the compensation to CPIC Hainan Company. CPIC Hainan Company's payment of insurance compensation to Haima Sales Company was evidenced not only by the compensation agreement but also by bank transfer vouchers and compensation receipts. The fact that CPIC Hainan Company paid insurance compensation to Haima Sales Company for the damaged Haima vehicles in question is affirmed.

(2) Regarding the cause of the fire accident. As to the "Inspection Report" issued by China Certification & Inspection Group Shanghai Co., Ltd. provided by CPIC Hainan Company, and the "Forensic Appraisal Report" issued by Zhejiang CIQ Appraisal Institute, the "Survey Report" issued by Shanghai Yuezhi Insurance Surveyors and Loss Adjusters Co., Ltd., and the "Inspection Report" issued by Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd. provided by COSCO Company, because the institutions and their appraisers/inspectors issuing the reports did not have the qualifications or competence to engage in the appraisal of the cause of fire accidents, violating the mandatory provisions of the state on fire accident appraisal and handling, and their appraisers and inspectors did not have the professional knowledge in fire appraisal, ships, and automotive electrical systems, the evidentiary effect of the above appraisal, inspection, and survey reports is not recognized; their determinations of the cause of the fire are not accepted.

Pursuant to Article 51 of the Fire Control Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 5 of the "Regulations on Fire Accident Investigation" promulgated by the Ministry of Public Security in April 2009, the only statutory body for fire accident investigation and handling is the public security fire authority; no other unit or department has the authority, qualifications, or capacity to investigate and handle fire accidents.

Pursuant to Article 9 of the "Regulations on the Investigation and Handling of Maritime Traffic Accidents of the People's Republic of China" and Article 64 of the Fire Control Law of the People's Republic of China, COSCO Company and the master of "Fuyuankou" had a statutory duty to report the fire accident and apply to the public security fire authority for an appraisal. Because COSCO Company failed to timely report and apply for investigation and appraisal by the public security fire authority, the cause of the fire accident in question could not be ascertained due to the passage of time. Therefore, the facts alleged by CPIC Hainan Company, COSCO Company, and Haima Sales Company that the fire accident in question was caused by "factors other than the vehicle itself" or "spontaneous combustion of the vehicle itself" are not established. As the cause of the fire accident cannot be determined, it is found that the cause of the fire accident in question is unknown.

(3) Regarding the determination of losses from the fire accident. The "Forensic Appraisal Report" issued by Zhejiang CIQ Appraisal Institute proved that the total loss amount of the damaged vehicles in question should be RMB 4,597,340. Although this institute had forensic appraisal qualifications, it did not have commodity price certification or appraisal qualifications. The evidentiary effect of this appraisal report and the loss amount of the damaged vehicles claimed by COSCO Company are not recognized.

The "Inspection Report" issued by Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Surveyors Co., Ltd. proved that the loss amount of the damaged vehicles should be RMB 4,566,500. However, this inspection institution had a conflict of interest with COSCO Company, its inspector Cai Zhaochun who signed the report did not have inspection or survey qualifications at the time, and he refused to sign the court transcript. Therefore, this inspection report is not accepted.

The Haikou Price Certification Center is the only institution in this case possessing the qualification for price judicial appraisal. The damaged vehicles in this case, being brand-new vehicles just off the production line, were subjected to high temperatures exceeding 1,000 degrees Celsius from the fire, causing varying degrees of qualitative changes in their paint, internal parts, etc., and posing potential quality risks. Not only could they not be repaired to the standard of new products, but the repair costs could not be unified. Moreover, if only simple cosmetic repairs were performed without any quality inspection and repair of internal parts, the result would not guarantee the normal and safe operation of the vehicles. The appraisal personnel of the Certification Center, starting from this actual condition of the damaged vehicles, used the market method to assess the loss. Compared with the repair method used in the evidence submitted by COSCO Company, this was more consistent with the actual circumstances of this case and also more reasonable. The description of the vehicle damage in the "Appraisal Report" was essentially consistent with the description by the appraisers of China Inspection and Certification Group Shanghai Co., Ltd., and its damage assessment result was also recognized by the appraisers of China Inspection and Certification Group Shanghai Co., Ltd.; the disposal price of the 443 damaged vehicles (excluding the 19 total loss vehicles) after repair, transportation, and assuming quality risks was approximately RMB 19 million. Even without considering the added repair and transportation costs, the price loss of the involved vehicles still reached approximately RMB 20 million, while the damage assessment amount in the appraisal report was over RMB 16 million, which was the closest to the actual disposal price of the vehicles. These all reflect the fairness and reasonableness of the appraisal report. Therefore, the evidentiary effect of the "Appraisal Report" issued by the Haikou Price Certification Center and its damage assessment conclusion for the damaged vehicles in this case, i.e., a loss amount of RMB 16,797,902, are affirmed.

CPIC Hainan Company, for the purpose of determining the nature, cause, and extent of the insured accident, and for the rescue and disposal of the damaged vehicles, after reaching an agreement with COSCO Company, arranged for the involved damaged vehicles to be shipped back from Shanghai to Haikou. The resulting expenses for dock storage, handling and cosmetic work, cleaning, transshipment, guarding, evaluation and appraisal, as well as the evidence preservation expenses incurred before litigation to preserve evidence, totaled RMB 697,888. The occurrence of the above expenses is evidenced by relevant agreements and invoices, and they were all necessary and reasonable, and are thus affirmed.

(4) Whether COSCO Company can enjoy the limitation of liability for maritime claims. The vessel "Fuyuankou" is a seaworthy vessel engaged in domestic coastal transportation. The loss of cargo in this case was not caused by the intentional act of COSCO Company or by its reckless act or omission with knowledge that such loss would probably result. Therefore, COSCO Company is entitled to limit its liability in accordance with the provisions of Chapter 11 of the Maritime Law of the PRC concerning limitation of liability for maritime claims and the provisions of the Ministry of Communications' "Regulations on Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims for Ships of Less than 300 Gross Tonnage and for Coastal Transportation and Coastal Operations Vessels." Based on the exchange rate of Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) against the Renminbi announced by the International Monetary Fund on October 23, 2009, the limitation amount for COSCO Company's maritime liability is RMB 8,243,897.

In summary, this case is a dispute over compensation for cargo damage under a waterway cargo transport contract. The "Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement" in this case is, in nature, a waterway cargo transport contract. Although it was signed between Jinpan Logistics Company and COSCO Company, because Jinpan Logistics Company is the agent of Haima Sales Company, the rights and obligations of Jinpan Logistics Company stipulated under that agreement should be enjoyed and borne by Haima Sales Company. Moreover, the agreement explicitly stipulated that Haima Sales Company, as the manufacturer of the transported vehicles, has the right to claim compensation for cargo loss from the carrier. Therefore, a waterway cargo transport contract relationship exists between Haima Sales Company and COSCO Company. CPIC Hainan Company is the insurer of the automobiles involved in this case. Having paid the insurance compensation and related rescue expenses to the insured, Haima Sales Company, it is entitled to exercise the right of subrogation to claim compensation from the carrier, COSCO Company. COSCO Company's argument that no waterway cargo transport contract relationship exists between Haima Sales Company and COSCO Company, and therefore CPIC Hainan Company has no right to exercise subrogation against it and is not an appropriate party, is not supported.

In this case, CPIC Hainan Company subrogates into the position of the insured, Haima Sales Company, under the waterway cargo transport contract. Therefore, it should be bound by the terms of that transport contract. The transport contract reflects the true intentions of the parties, its content is clear and standardized, and it does not violate the mandatory provisions of national laws or administrative regulations. It is therefore confirmed as valid. COSCO Company, as the carrier for the cargo transportation on this voyage, has a period of responsibility from the time the goods are loaded on board until the time they are discharged. According to Article 48 of the "Regulations on Domestic Waterway Cargo Transport" and Article 311 of the Contract Law of the PRC, a carrier engaged in coastal cargo transport bears a relatively strict liability for compensation. Except for cargo loss caused by force majeure, the inherent nature of the goods, or the fault of the shipper or consignee, the carrier shall bear liability for compensation. Moreover, the carrier bears the burden of proof for its grounds of exemption. During the voyage of the "Fuyuankou," a fire occurred in its hold, causing damage to the automobiles it was carrying. Although COSCO Company claimed that the fire accident was caused by the spontaneous combustion of the automobiles delivered by the shipper, it could not provide evidence to prove that the fire accident resulted from spontaneous combustion or that it fell under other grounds for exemption specified in the "Regulations on Domestic Waterway Cargo Transport" and the Contract Law of the PRC. Furthermore, because COSCO Company failed to promptly report and apply to the public security fire department for investigation and appraisal, the cause of this fire accident could not be determined due to the passage of time. Therefore, COSCO Company's claim for exemption is not established. COSCO Company shall bear liability for compensating the losses and interest suffered by CPIC Hainan Company in this case.

The vessel "Fuyuankou" is a seaworthy vessel engaged in domestic coastal transportation. COSCO Company is entitled to limit its liability according to the provisions of Chapter 11 of the Maritime Law of the PRC concerning limitation of liability for maritime claims and the provisions of the Ministry of Communications' "Regulations on Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims for Ships of Less than 300 Gross Tonnage and for Coastal Transportation and Coastal Operations Vessels." CPIC Hainan Company's claim for losses exceeding the limitation amount is not supported.

Pursuant to Articles 311 and 403 of the Contract Law of the PRC, Chapter 11 of the Maritime Law of the PRC, and Articles 240(1), 252(1), and 277 of the Maritime Law of the PRC, the first-instance judgment ruled as follows: 1. COSCO Company shall compensate CPIC Hainan Company for economic losses in the amount of RMB 8,243,897; 2. CPIC Hainan Company's other claims against COSCO Company are dismissed.

Both COSCO Company and CPIC Hainan Company, being dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Hainan High People's Court.

COSCO Company appealed, arguing: 1. No waterway cargo transport contract relationship exists between CPIC Hainan Company's insured, Haima Sales Company, and COSCO Company; 2. The fire accident was caused by the spontaneous combustion of the automobiles, so COSCO Company is not liable for compensation; 3. CPIC Hainan Company failed to meet its burden of proof to effectively demonstrate the actual loss of the alleged damaged vehicles. It requested the revocation of the first-instance judgment, a remand for retrial, or an alternative judgment dismissing CPIC Hainan Company's claims.

CPIC Hainan Company appealed, arguing: The first-instance judgment erred by not calculating interest on the limitation amount for maritime claims. The remaining findings of fact were clear and the application of law was correct.

The Hainan High People's Court confirmed the facts found by the Haikou Maritime Court.

Additional facts were found: 1. Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Appraisal Co., Ltd. possesses appraisal qualifications and business scope. Its registered capital is RMB 2 million, with shareholders Huang Yaquan, Zhang Jindai, Huang Anhua, and Huang Anwen. Huang Yaquan and Zhang Jindai each hold 30% of the shares, while Huang Anhua and Huang Anwen each hold 20%. Huang Yaquan is also the director of Guangdong Hengyun Law Firm. Huang Hui, the agent ad litem for COSCO Company in this case, is a practicing lawyer at Guangdong Hengyun Law Firm, and Chen Qun is a legal assistant at the same firm. Cai Zhaochun obtained his insurance appraisal qualification on September 21, 2008, while the "Inspection Report" issued by Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Appraisal Co., Ltd. was dated August 13, 2008. During the inspection period, Cai Zhaochun did not have valid insurance appraisal qualifications. The names Cai Zhaochun and Han Junming were printed on the "Inspection Report" but without handwritten signatures, and the company's legal representative, Zhou Cuiying, did not sign it either. 2. The Quality Management Department and the Operation Management Department of FAW-Haima Automobile Co., Ltd. are two internal departments of FAW-Haima Automobile Co., Ltd.

Based on the arguments of the parties and the facts of the case, the Hainan High People's Court analyzed and determined the disputed issues as follows:

(1) Whether CPIC Hainan Company has the subject qualification to file this lawsuit. On January 1, 2007, Jinpan Logistics Company and COSCO Company signed the "Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement." This agreement represents the true intention of both parties, its content does not violate laws or mandatory regulations, and it is a valid agreement that all parties should abide by and perform. Haima Sales Company is the sales management enterprise and owner of the involved vehicles. The agreement between Haima Sales Company and Jinpan Logistics Company stipulated that Haima Sales Company entrusted Jinpan Logistics Company with the transportation of Haima automobiles. According to Article 42 of the Maritime Law of the PRC concerning the definition and scope of "shipper," Haima Sales Company, having entrusted another person to deliver the goods to a carrier related to the maritime cargo transport contract on its behalf, is a shipper. Paragraphs 8 of Article 17 and 1 of Article 22 of the "Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement" grant Haima Sales Company the right to directly claim compensation from COSCO Company when COSCO Company breaches the agreement for non-excusable reasons, causing losses to Jinpan Logistics Company, its affiliated companies, or the shipper. Therefore, Haima Sales Company, based on its status as the sales management enterprise under the "Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement" and its identity as a shipper, has the right to claim compensation from COSCO Company.

On April 10, 2008, the insured, Haima Sales Company, and the insurer, CPIC Hainan Company, reached an "Insurance Compensation Agreement." The accounting receipts, check stubs, and compensation receipts provided by CPIC Hainan Company indicate that it actually paid RMB 16,395,960 in compensation. After compensating Haima Sales Company for the loss of the involved vehicles, CPIC Hainan Company is entitled to succeed to the contractual rights of Haima Sales Company under the "Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement" and claim compensation from COSCO Company. Therefore, CPIC Hainan Company is an appropriate litigation subject in this case. COSCO Company's argument that CPIC Hainan Company is not the appropriate litigation subject is not supported.

(2) Determination of the cause of the fire accident. Fire accident investigation is a public management function. No unit may exercise this function without authorization from laws or administrative regulations. Article 51 of the Fire Prevention Law of the PRC, Article 5 of the "Regulations on Fire Accident Investigation" issued by the Ministry of Public Security in April 2009, and Article 9(3) of the "Regulations on Investigation and Handling of Maritime Traffic Accidents of the PRC" all clearly stipulate that the legal body responsible for fire accident investigation and handling is the public security fire department. No other organs or units are authorized by laws or administrative regulations to exercise this function. Article 23 of the "Regulations on Fire Prevention Management for Transport Vessels" and Article 64 of the Fire Prevention Law of the PRC explicitly stipulate the duty of individuals and organizations to report fires. After the fire, the captain of the "Fuyuankou" did not report the incident or apply to the public security fire department for appraisal, bearing an undeniable responsibility for the failure to ascertain the cause of the fire. Any plan or agreement involving non-reporting or non-appraisal is illegal and invalid. The first-instance court's determination that COSCO Company and the captain of the "Fuyuankou" had a legal duty to report the fire accident and apply to the public security fire department for appraisal is accurate.

To prove the cause of the fire, CPIC Hainan Company submitted the "Appraisal Report" issued by China Inspection and Certification Group Shanghai Co., Ltd., and COSCO Company submitted the "Judicial Appraisal Report" issued by Zhejiang Entry-Exit Inspection and Quarantine Appraisal Institute, the "Appraisal Report" issued by Shanghai Yuezhi Insurance Appraisal Co., Ltd., and the "Inspection Report" issued by Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Appraisal Co., Ltd. The institutions that issued these reports do not possess the professional qualification or business scope for fire cause identification and do not have the social public management function. They violate the provisions of the aforementioned laws and regulations that the right to investigate and determine the cause of fires should be exercised by public security fire departments. The conclusions they issued lack legality and probative force. Article 54 of the Maritime Law of the PRC stipulates that the carrier bears the burden of proving the grounds for exemption from liability for cargo loss or damage occurring during the carriage. COSCO Company failed to request the public security fire department to investigate the cause of the fire. It therefore bears the consequence of failing to meet its burden of proof on the fire cause. According to Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings," it shall bear the adverse consequences and is liable for compensation for the losses caused by this fire.

(3) Determination of the vehicle losses caused by the fire. Article 23(2) of the "Regulations on Fire Accident Investigation" stipulates: "The public security fire department may, as needed, entrust a price appraisal institution established according to law to assess the direct property loss from the fire." Article 26 further stipulates: "The public security fire department shall review the following matters concerning the appraisal opinions provided by the damaged entity or individual and issued by a price appraisal institution: (1) whether the appraisal institution and appraiser have the necessary qualifications; (2) whether the appraisal institution and appraiser have affixed their seals or signatures; (3) whether the basis for the appraisal opinion is sufficient; (4) whether there are other circumstances affecting the correctness of the appraisal opinion. Appraisal opinions that meet the requirements may be used as evidence; those that do not meet the requirements shall not be admitted." Therefore, court may admit as evidence of fire losses appraisal opinions that meet the review requirements of Article 26 of the "Regulations on Fire Accident Investigation." COSCO Company's argument that organizations other than the public security fire department lack the qualification or authority to compile fire loss statistics is not supported.

Zhejiang Entry-Exit Inspection and Quarantine Appraisal Institute does not possess price appraisal qualifications or a business scope covering loss determination. The loss determination in the "Judicial Appraisal Report" it issued is not confirmed. Although Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Appraisal Co., Ltd. possesses price appraisal qualifications and business scope, Cai Zhaochun, one of the signatories of the "Inspection Report," had not obtained valid insurance appraisal qualifications before the report was issued. The legal representative of the company, Zhou Cuiying, did not sign the "Inspection Report." Therefore, the report lacks legality. When Cai Zhaochun appeared in court at first instance to be questioned, he refused to sign the trial transcript. Furthermore, Mr. Huang Yaquan, the director of Guangdong Hengyun Law Firm, where COSCO Company's agent ad litem works, is the largest shareholder of Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Appraisal Co., Ltd., and Mr. Huang Yaquan had previously been entrusted by COSCO Company to issue a "Statement" to Jinpan Logistics Company and CPIC Hainan Company on March 5, 2008, regarding the handling of this fire accident. The first-instance court's determination that a conflict of interest exists between Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Appraisal Co., Ltd. and COSCO Company is not improper. Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Appraisal Co., Ltd., being an interested party that should have withdrawn from the appraisal process, failed to do so, violating the recusal provisions of Article 20 of the "Procedural Rules for Judicial Appraisal." The validity of the "Inspection Report" issued by this company is not recognized.

The Haikou Price Certification Center possesses the qualifications for price judicial appraisal and corresponding business scope. The "Appraisal Report" it issued meets the review conditions required by Article 26 of the "Regulations on Fire Accident Investigation." Although COSCO Company pointed out that there were VIN code errors in the report, this defect does not constitute a circumstance affecting the correctness of the appraisal opinion. The "Appraisal Report" is thus affirmed. The loss suffered by the involved vehicles in this fire is RMB 16,797,902.

CPIC Hainan Company, for the purpose of determining the nature, cause, and extent of the insured accident, and for the rescue and disposal of the damaged vehicles, after reaching an agreement with COSCO Company, arranged for the involved damaged vehicles to be shipped back from Shanghai to Haikou, incurring expenses for dock storage, handling and cosmetic work, cleaning, etc., totaling RMB 697,888.

In summary, COSCO Company shall be liable for compensating the losses suffered by CPIC Hainan Company in this case, amounting to RMB 17,093,848, plus interest. The vessel "Fuyuankou" is a seaworthy vessel engaged in domestic coastal transportation. There is no evidence in this case that the cargo loss was caused by the intentional act of COSCO Company or by its reckless act or omission with knowledge that such loss would probably result. According to Articles 58 and 59 of the Maritime Law of the PRC, COSCO Company is entitled to limit its liability for maritime claims. Pursuant to Article 210(2) of the Maritime Law of the PRC, Article 4 of the "Regulations on Limitation of Liability for Maritime Claims for Ships of Less than 300 Gross Tonnage and for Coastal Transportation and Coastal Operations Vessels," and the SDR exchange rate determined by the first-instance court, COSCO Company shall bear liability to CPIC Hainan Company in the amount of RMB 8,243,897.

(4) Regarding CPIC Hainan Company's claim for interest. According to Article 213 of the Maritime Law of the PRC, interest arises only when the debtor constitutes a limitation fund. Since COSCO Company did not constitute a limitation fund in this case, CPIC Hainan Company's request for COSCO Company to pay interest by reference to the situation where a fund had been constituted is not expressly provided for by law and is not supported. The first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact and correct application of law. Pursuant to Article 153(1)(i) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the second-instance judgment ruled: Appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed.

COSCO Company, dissatisfied with the second-instance judgment, applied to this Court for retrial, arguing: 1. The second-instance judgment applied the law incorrectly. This case concerns a dispute over a maritime cargo transport contract between ports within the PRC, yet the second-instance judgment applied the provisions of Chapter 4 of the Maritime Law of the PRC when determining issues such as "whether CPIC Hainan Company has subject qualification to sue" and "the cause of the fire accident"; 2. The "Agreement" signed between Jinpan Logistics Company and Haima Sales Company is not a mandate contract. Haima Sales Company cannot claim damages for breach of contract against COSCO Company based on the "Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement." The stipulation in Paragraph 8 of Article 17 of the "Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement" should not create a "liability for breach of contract" for COSCO Company towards a third party; 3. The second-instance judgment's determination of the burden of proof regarding the fire cause lacks factual and legal basis. Jinpan Logistics Company should bear full responsibility for the accident; 4. The second-instance judgment's determination of the loss amount for the damaged vehicles lacks factual and legal basis. COSCO Company requested the revocation of the first-instance and second-instance judgments, a judgment dismissing all claims of CPIC Hainan Company, and that CPIC Hainan Company bear all litigation costs of the first and second instances.

Pacific Insurance Hainan Company argued in its defense: 1. This case should be governed by the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and the Rules for Domestic Carriage of Goods by Water, and the second-instance judgment erred in applying the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China; 2. Haima Sales Company was entitled to claim damages for breach of contract against COSCO Company based on the Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement between Jinpan Logistics Company and COSCO Company. The second-instance judgment correctly found that Haima Sales Company could directly claim against COSCO Company pursuant to Article 17, paragraph 8 of the Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement; 3. The second-instance judgment correctly held that COSCO Company bore the burden of proof for exemption from liability for losses caused by the fire; 4. The second-instance judgment's determination of the losses of the damaged vehicles at issue was well-founded.

Haima Sales Company argued in its defense: 1. The relationship between Haima Sales Company and Jinpan Logistics Company was one of principal and agent, which was known to COSCO Company. Haima Sales Company could bring an action for breach of contract against COSCO Company, and Pacific Insurance Hainan Company had lawful standing as a party to the litigation; 2. The second-instance judgment correctly found that Haima Sales Company was entitled to claim against COSCO Company under Article 17, paragraph 8 of the Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement; 3. The cause of the fire at issue could not be determined because COSCO Company failed to fulfill its statutory obligations. COSCO Company bore the liability for failing to meet its burden of proof regarding the cause of the fire; 4. The second-instance judgment correctly refused to admit the evidentiary value of the Inspection Report issued by Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Adjusters Co., Ltd. and the Judicial Appraisal Report issued by Zhejiang Entry-Exit Inspection and Quarantine Bureau, as well as the loss amounts derived therefrom.

During the hearing of this case, COSCO Company submitted, as new evidence, the waterway cargo receipts for the return shipment of the 390 vehicles at issue from Shanghai to Haikou and the cargo booking notes for 462 vehicles, to prove that the transport from Shanghai to Haikou was an independent waterway cargo transport contract. Pacific Insurance Hainan Company and Haima Sales Company both challenged the authenticity of the above new evidence and argued that, although the return shipment did occur, it was merely a step in the parties' handling of the issue, not an independent act.

Pacific Insurance Hainan Company submitted four pieces of new evidence: 1. A statement from Haima Sales Company; 2. A statement from Jinpan Logistics Company and a copy of its business license; the above evidence was used to prove that the relationship between Haima Sales Company and Jinpan Logistics Company was one of principal and agent. 3. A statement from Haima Sales Company regarding the numbering of Haima commercial vehicles, used to prove the principles and methods of numbering Haima commercial vehicles; 4. Published materials of COSCO Company, used to prove that COSCO Company provided transport services for the manufacturer of Haima commercial vehicles, rather than for Jinpan Logistics Company. COSCO Company did not challenge the authenticity of the above evidence but challenged its relevance to this case, arguing that Haima Sales Company and Jinpan Logistics Company were affiliated companies with an interest in the matter, and therefore evidence items 1 and 2, which corroborated each other, were invalid. Evidence item 4 consisted of promotional materials of the company and did not constitute an explanation of the specific contract in this case. Haima Sales Company did not challenge the above evidence.

Upon review, this Court finds that the waybills and cargo booking notes from Shanghai to Haikou submitted by COSCO Company were all copies, and both Pacific Insurance Hainan Company and Haima Sales Company challenged their authenticity. Therefore, this Court does not admit them. The four pieces of new evidence submitted by Pacific Insurance Hainan Company are admitted by this Court because COSCO Company and Haima Sales Company did not challenge their authenticity.

The following facts are found through trial by this Court: The basic facts found by the court of first instance are supported by relevant evidence, and this Court confirms them.

This Court is of the opinion: This case is a dispute over compensation for cargo damage arising from a waterway cargo transport contract. The Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement concluded between Jinpan Logistics Company and COSCO Company is lawful, valid, and binding on all parties. The issues in dispute in this case are: (1) Whether there was an error in the application of law in the second-instance judgment; (2) Whether Haima Sales Company could claim damages for breach of contract against COSCO Company based on the Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement, i.e., whether Pacific Insurance Hainan Company had lawful standing as a party to the litigation; (3) Whether the second-instance judgment's determination of the burden of proof for the cause of the fire and liability for cargo damage compensation in this case was correct; (4) Whether the second-instance judgment's determination of the amount of loss of the damaged vehicles at issue was correct.

Regarding the issue of the application of law. This case arose from a dispute caused by damage to the vehicles during the sea transport period when COSCO Company performed the Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement it concluded and was responsible for carrying the vehicles at issue. It is a dispute over compensation for cargo damage under a maritime cargo transport contract. The Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, as a special law, should apply preferentially. However, the transport at issue was from Haikou to Shanghai, which is maritime transport between ports of the People's Republic of China. Article 2, paragraph 2 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China provides: "The provisions of Chapter IV of this Code concerning contracts of carriage of goods by sea shall not apply to maritime cargo transport between ports of the People's Republic of China." Therefore, Chapter IV of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China does not apply to this case. This case should be governed by provisions of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China other than those in Chapter IV. For matters not provided for in the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, the relevant provisions of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China shall apply.

When the Hainan High People's Court, in its second-instance judgment, determined the issue of "whether Pacific Insurance Hainan Company had standing as a party to the litigation," it applied Article 42 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China concerning the concept and scope of a shipper, and found that Haima Sales Company was a person who entrusted another to deliver the goods on its behalf to a carrier in connection with a contract of carriage of goods by sea. When determining the issue of "the cause of the fire at issue," it applied Article 54 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China concerning the carrier's burden of proof for damage caused by other causes, and found that COSCO Company bore the liability for failing to meet its burden of proof regarding the cause of the fire. When determining the issue of "the vehicle losses caused by the fire," it applied Articles 58 and 59 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China and found that COSCO Company was entitled to limit its liability for maritime claims. The above-applied provisions are all provisions of Chapter IV of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China. Therefore, the second-instance judgment was clearly erroneous in the application of law and should be corrected.

Regarding the issue of Pacific Insurance Hainan Company's standing as a party to the litigation. On December 31, 2006, Haima Sales Company and Jinpan Logistics Company concluded an Agreement stipulating: Haima Sales Company entrusts to Jinpan Logistics Company the logistics, warehousing, transport, and other matters of Haima commercial vehicles, and Jinpan Logistics Company is responsible for the logistics, warehousing, transport, and other work of Haima commercial vehicles entrusted by Haima Sales Company. On January 1, 2007, Jinpan Logistics Company and COSCO Company concluded the Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement, Article 1 of which stipulates: Jinpan Logistics Company designates COSCO Company as the carrier for the waterway transport of vehicles from Haikou to Shanghai, and COSCO Company shall use its roll-on/roll-off vessels to carry out the waterway transport of vehicles from Haikou to Shanghai for Jinpan Logistics Company. Article 17, paragraph 8 stipulates: If, due to a cause for which exemption is not available, COSCO Company breaches the agreement, causing losses to Jinpan Logistics Company (including affiliates of Jinpan Logistics Company and the shipper) or the vehicle manufacturer, Jinpan Logistics Company or the vehicle manufacturer is entitled to claim compensation. This Court is of the opinion that, according to the terms of the agreement, at the time of contracting, COSCO Company already knew that the actual shipper of the goods it carried was the "vehicle manufacturer," and the agreement expressly provided that the "vehicle manufacturer" had the right to claim compensation against COSCO Company if it suffered losses due to COSCO Company's breach of the transport contract. This term represents the unanimous intention of the parties to the agreement, stipulating that a third party may directly claim against COSCO Company, and it is binding on all parties. This term does not fall within the circumstance described in Article 64 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "the parties may agree that the debtor shall perform the obligations to a third party." COSCO Company's assertion that Haima Sales Company had no right to file a lawsuit based on the Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement lacks legal basis. Article 22, paragraph 1 of the Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement stipulates: "Vehicle manufacturer" means the manufacturer of the vehicles to be carried or the enterprise responsible for the sales management of the vehicles to be carried. According to the Exclusive Distributor Agreement, Haima Sales Company was the sales management enterprise and the owner of the vehicles at issue. Therefore, Haima Sales Company was entitled to claim against COSCO Company based on the Vehicle Transport Cooperation Agreement. The insurer, Pacific Insurance Hainan Company, after paying insurance compensation to Haima Sales Company, acquired the right of subrogation in accordance with the law. The second-instance judgment's finding that Pacific Insurance Hainan Company had lawful standing as a party to the litigation was not improper.

Regarding the burden of proof for the cause of the fire and liability for cargo damage compensation. According to the Maritime Report and the Deck Log of the vessel "Fuyuankou" at issue, a fire broke out in the cargo hold during the voyage from Haikou to Shanghai, causing damage to the vehicles being carried. All parties agreed on this fact. This case is not governed by the provisions of Chapter IV of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China and should be governed by the relevant provisions of Chapter 17 (Transport Contracts) of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China to determine liability. Article 311 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The carrier shall be liable for the damage or loss of the goods occurring during the carriage, unless the carrier proves that the damage or loss was caused by force majeure, the inherent nature of the goods, reasonable wear and tear, or the fault of the shipper or the consignee." Therefore, as the carrier under the cargo transport contract, COSCO Company should be liable for compensation for the loss of the goods occurring during the carriage, unless it proves the existence of statutory grounds for exemption. COSCO Company asserted that the fire at issue was caused by spontaneous combustion of the vehicles and should bear the corresponding burden of proof. The second-instance judgment's determination of the burden of proof for the cause of the fire was not improper.

To prove the cause of the fire at issue, Pacific Insurance Hainan Company submitted an Appraisal Report issued by China Certification & Inspection Group Shanghai Co., Ltd., and COSCO Company submitted a Judicial Appraisal Report issued by Zhejiang Entry-Exit Inspection and Quarantine Appraisal Institute, an Average Survey Report issued by Shanghai Yuezhi Insurance Adjusters Co., Ltd., and an Inspection Report issued by Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Adjusters Co., Ltd. This Court is of the opinion that Article 6 of the Provisions on the Investigation of Fire Accidents of the Ministry of Public Security provides: "The investigation of fire accidents shall be conducted by the fire protection agencies of the public security organs." Article 10 provides: "Fire protection agencies at all levels shall be equipped with full-time or part-time fire accident investigators. Fire accident investigators shall obtain the corresponding qualifications in accordance with the relevant provisions on the qualification management of public security fire protection supervisors." Therefore, the agency responsible for investigating and handling fire accidents should be the fire protection agency of the public security organ, and investigators should have the corresponding qualifications. The agencies entrusted by COSCO Company and Pacific Insurance Hainan Company were not fire protection agencies of the public security organs, and the inspectors and appraisers did not have the qualifications for fire accident investigation. The second-instance judgment's refusal to admit the findings on the cause of the fire made in the appraisal, inspection, and average survey reports submitted by COSCO Company and Pacific Insurance Hainan Company was not improper. After the fire occurred, because COSCO Company did not report to the fire protection agency of the public security organ or the port authority, the cause of the fire could not be determined. COSCO Company failed to submit sufficient evidence to prove that it had statutory grounds for exemption from liability for the fire. The second-instance judgment, by holding COSCO Company liable for the adverse consequences of failing to meet its burden of proof, and ordering COSCO Company to bear compensation liability for the losses caused by the fire, was not improper.

The facts found in the original trial show that on December 23, 2007, the vessel "Fuyuankou" arrived at Shanghai Haitong Wharf. A fire broke out during the voyage, causing damage to the vehicles being carried. After consultation, COSCO Company and Jinpan Logistics Company signed a vehicle return shipment agreement. Article 1 of that agreement stipulates: The follow-up handling of the fire in the cargo hold of the "Fuyuankou" on December 21, 2007, shall be resolved by the parties through friendly negotiation or other means. Article 2 stipulates: The 462 commercial vehicles involved in the accident (including 72 temporarily stored in the hold) shall be shipped back to Haikou on the "Fuyuankou". Taken together with the Maritime Report and Deck Log, this return shipment agreement sufficiently proves the occurrence of the fire and the resulting damage to the vehicles. COSCO Company's assertion that the absence of a vehicle discharge acceptance record means the cargo damage cannot be proved lacks factual and legal basis. Article 5 of the return shipment agreement stipulates: After the vehicles are delivered at the port of discharge, COSCO Company's transport responsibility for the Shanghai-to-Haikou leg shall terminate, and the risk shall transfer to Jinpan Logistics Company. COSCO Company argued that this provision indicates that the return shipment agreement has been fully performed, the risk of loss of the goods has been transferred to Jinpan Logistics Company, and COSCO Company should not bear compensation liability. This Court is of the opinion that the waterway transport from Shanghai to Haikou referred to in the return shipment agreement is indeed an independent transport contract, but the transfer of risk liability stipulated in Article 5 only concerns the risk liability that may arise during the transport from Shanghai to Haikou. The signing of the return shipment agreement and the fact of the return shipment cannot be deemed as Jinpan Logistics Company's waiver of its claim against COSCO Company for the fire, nor can it be deemed as Jinpan Logistics Company's tacit acceptance of COSCO Company's assertion that the fire was caused by spontaneous combustion of the vehicles. The petitioner, COSCO Company, asserted that Jinpan Logistics Company's unloading and return shipment actions both proved that the transport contract had been fully performed and that Jinpan Logistics Company was willing to bear the liability for the cargo damage itself. This assertion lacks sufficient factual and legal basis.

Regarding the amount of vehicle losses. To prove the extent of the damage to the vehicles, COSCO Company submitted a Judicial Appraisal Report issued by Zhejiang Entry-Exit Inspection and Quarantine Appraisal Institute and an Inspection Report issued by Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Adjusters Co., Ltd. The business scope of Zhejiang Entry-Exit Inspection and Quarantine Appraisal Institute does not include price appraisal, and it does not have the qualifications for commodity price appraisal. Guangzhou Haizheng Insurance Adjusters Co., Ltd., as an interested party, did not recuse itself from the appraisal process, and the signatory of its Inspection Report, Cai Zhaochun, did not have the corresponding appraisal qualifications at the time the report was issued and refused to sign the trial transcript of the first instance. The second-instance judgment's refusal to admit the above two appraisal and inspection reports was not clearly improper.

To prove the extent of the damage to the vehicles, Pacific Insurance Hainan Company submitted a series of evidence, including a Valuation Report issued by Haikou Price Certification Center, a Vehicle Stacking Agreement and invoice, a Vehicle Cleaning Agreement and invoice, and transport invoices. To prove the actual disposition of the damaged vehicles, upon COSCO Company's application and at the request of the first-instance court, Haima Sales Company additionally provided the sales contracts and invoices for the actual disposition of the damaged vehicles at issue after repair. The Haikou Price Certification Center entrusted by Pacific Insurance Hainan Company has the qualifications and business scope for judicial appraisal of prices. The second-instance judgment's recognition of the evidentiary value of this Appraisal Report was not improper.

According to the return shipment agreement, all parties agreed that 462 commercial vehicles were damaged in the fire, and all accident vehicles were shipped back to Haikou by COSCO Company and unloaded at Haikou Xiuying Port Wharf. To determine the nature, cause, and extent of the insured accident, it was not improper for Pacific Insurance Hainan Company to entrust Haikou Price Certification Center to inspect the accident vehicles. COSCO Company's assertion that the Valuation Report has no factual relevance to the disputed cargo damage in this case lacks sufficient factual basis.

The damaged vehicles in this case were new vehicles. After being subjected to high temperatures from the fire, they had potential quality risks, and the value of the repaired vehicles differed significantly from that of new vehicles. The Valuation Report issued by Haikou Price Certification Center used the market approach for loss assessment, which is more realistic and reasonable than determining the loss based on repair costs, as advocated by COSCO Company. Furthermore, taken together with the sales contracts and invoices for the actual disposition of the damaged vehicles at issue after repair, submitted by Haima Sales Company, the second-instance judgment's recognition of the loss assessment conclusion in the Valuation Report, setting the amount of vehicle loss at RMB 16,797,902, was not improper. COSCO Company did not submit sufficient contrary evidence, and its assertion that the second-instance judgment's determination of the loss amount was erroneous lacks sufficient factual and legal basis.

In summary, as the carrier under the cargo transport contract at issue, COSCO Company should bear compensation liability for the loss of the vehicles caused by the fire that occurred during the carriage. The vessel "Fuyuankou" is a seaworthy vessel engaged in domestic coastal transport. According to Article 204 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China, COSCO Company is entitled to limit its liability for maritime claims. The second-instance judgment's application of Articles 42, 54, 58, and 59 of the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China constituted an error in the application of law and should be corrected. However, the facts found were clear, and the result of the judgment was correct. This Court affirms the judgment. Pursuant to Article 186, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

The Civil Judgment (2010) Qiong Min San Zhong Zi No. 2 of the Hainan High People's Court is affirmed.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Wang Shumei
